recent_articles.title: Sulur minor girl abduction and murder: Law and order a serious concern in T.N., says Udhayanidhi Stalin - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Udhayanidhi Stalin**, leader of the Opposition, expressed concern over 30 major crimes within 12 days of the new government assuming office. These incidents include sexual violence, ganja smuggling, and the abduction and murder of a minor girl in Coimbatore. **Stalin** called for swift justice for the victim's family and urged the Chief Minister to prioritize law and order to prevent future incidents.

recent_articles.title: Historic shift: Vijay’s Cabinet marks Tamil Nadu’s best SC representation till date - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **C. Joseph Vijay**, the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, has appointed seven members from the Scheduled Caste (SC) community to his Cabinet. This marks a significant increase in SC representation compared to previous Cabinets.  Political analyst Stalin Rajangam believes this is a positive step towards inclusivity and sets a benchmark for future governments. However, Punitha Pandiyan, former Vice President of the Tamil Nadu SC/ST Commission, argues that celebrating this development trivializes SC politics.

recent_articles.title: 22 Ministers aged below 50: Cabinet signals generational shift in Tamil Nadu politics - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Tamil Nadu government's Cabinet has seen a significant shift in age composition, with the 2026 TVK Cabinet featuring the youngest average age among the three governments examined.  **C. Joseph Vijay**, the Chief Minister of this government, is 51 years old and his cabinet features the youngest Ministers at just 28 and 29 years old. The 2026 TVK Cabinet has nine Ministers in their 30s, followed by a senior tier of seven Ministers in their 50s, three in their 60s, and only one in the 70-80 age bracket.  This contrasts with the 2021 DMK Cabinet which was heavily dominated by older leaders.

recent_articles.title: Udhayanidhi clarifies stand on Sanatana - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Udhayanidhi Stalin**, leader of the DMK youth wing, defended his statement in the Tamil Nadu Assembly that "Sanatana that divides people should be destroyed," saying it did not mean people should stop visiting temples. He insisted he was echoing the views of historical figures like **Periyar E.V. Ramasamy**, **B.R. Ambedkar**, and **C. N. Annadurai**.  He stated that equal rights should be given to all, not just in temples but throughout society.

recent_articles.title: DMK boycotts floor test; urges CM to continue with Dravidian model welfare schemes - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Udhayanidhi Stalin**, leader of the **Tamil Nadu** opposition, led his party members in a boycott of a confidence motion presented by Chief Minister **C. Joseph Vijay**.  The walkout occurred after **Stalin** stated that the majority did not vote for the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK).

recent_articles.title: Jammu and Kashmir leaders ask Omar Abdullah government to follow steps of Tamil Nadu CM Vijay on liquor ban - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Dr. Farooq Abdullah**, president of the **National Conference**, stated that a complete ban on liquor sales in **Jammu and Kashmir** is not feasible due to revenue loss concerns, while opposition parties like the **Peoples Democratic Party (PDP)** and **J&K Apni Party** urged the government to follow Tamil Nadu's example by closing down liquor shops.  **Mirwaiz Umar Farooq**, the Kashmir chief cleric, argued that alcohol consumption is socially and religiously discouraged in the region and called for a complete ban on liquor sales to combat drug networks and societal harm.

recent_articles.title: BJP targets DMK leader Udhayanidhi Stalin over Sanatana Dharma remarks - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** condemned **Udhayanidhi Stalin**, a DMK leader, for his remarks on Sanatana Dharma in the Tamil Nadu Assembly.  **G. Kishan Reddy**, Union Minister for Coal and Mines, accused the DMK of "poisonous politics" and "anti-Hindu rhetoric." The BJP also criticized the Congress party's support for Stalin's comments and questioned **Vijay**, the newly elected Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, on his silence regarding the issue.

recent_articles.title: ​Split wide open: On the AIADMK, Tamil Nadu politics - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **AIADMK**, the principal opposition party in Tamil Nadu, is facing a split after a second consecutive election defeat.  **C. Joseph Vijay**, the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, has indicated his support for the dissident group led by former Ministers **C.Ve. Shanmugam** and **S.P. Velumani**. The dissidents have announced their intention to support the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government.  The Palaniswami camp claims that all 47 legislators gave written consent for **Edappadi K. Palaniswami** as the AIADMK legislature party leader, citing a Supreme Court verdict in the Shiv Sena case. The Assembly Speaker will need to assess the merits of both groups' claims and may soon have to draw on his experience and legal advice.

recent_articles.title: Floor test will be smooth; have received letters from EPS, Velumani factions: T.N. Assembly Speaker - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **J.C.D. Prabhakar**, the new Speaker of the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly, assured that Wednesday's floor test will be smooth and successful. He acknowledged receiving letters from two rival AIADMK groups regarding the election of their Legislature Party Leader.  He plans to organize an orientation program for first-time legislators and will continue to follow established assembly conventions. **Prabhakar** expressed his confidence in the Chief Minister's majority and stated that he will oversee a smooth floor test. He has been involved in Tamil Nadu politics since 1972, serving as a legislator, secretary of the AIADMK, and later under **J. Jayalalithaa**.

recent_articles.title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay gives maiden speech in Assembly after TVK win - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **C. Joseph Vijay**, the new **Tamil Nadu Chief Minister**, delivered his maiden speech in the Assembly, emphasizing social equity and cooperation.  He congratulated **J.C.D. Prabhakar**, elected Speaker, and outlined priorities for governance, welfare, youth development, and transparency. The government also announced the closure of 717 TASMAC liquor shops within 500 meters of educational institutions and places of worship.

recent_articles.title: Vijay, Udhayanidhi, Palaniswami take oath as MLAs in Tamil Nadu; J.C.D. Prabhakar nominated for Speaker post - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **C. Joseph Vijay**, the new **Tamil Nadu Chief Minister**, and his cabinet colleagues took their oaths in the 17th Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly on Monday, May 11, 2026.  The assembly's strength is now 233 following the resignation of Vijay from a second seat.  **M.V. Karuppaiah**, the Pro-tem Speaker, administered the oath to **Vijay** and other members. The election for Speaker and Deputy Speaker will be held on Tuesday, May 12, 2026.

recent_articles.title: The emerging Rahul Gandhi-Vijay political partnership - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Gandhi**, Congress leader, attended the swearing-in ceremony of **C. Joseph Vijay**'s new **Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam** government in Chennai. The event signaled a potential shift in the political landscape between the Congress and the DMK, with **Gandhi** expressing support for **Vijay** and their relationship mirroring that shared by former allies **M.K. Stalin** and **Gandhi**.  The TVK's success may bolster the Congress's influence in southern India.

recent_articles.title: ​No detours: On the Tamil Nadu elections, post-poll outcome - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)**, led by C. Joseph Vijay, formed a government after securing the support of **Congress**, **CPI(M)**, **CPI**, **VCK**, and **IUML** parties, despite falling short of a majority. The Governor's decision to disregard the Sarkaria Commission framework and Supreme Court rulings regarding the strength of a ministry was criticized.  The Congress's alliance with the TVK is seen as opportunistic, potentially jeopardizing their decades-long alliance with the DMK.

recent_articles.title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay's maiden speech on his new government in Tamil Nadu - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **C. Joseph Vijay**, the newly sworn-in Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, outlined his vision for a government focused on transparency, safety of women, and law and order. He pledged to address public debt and promised accountability in the use of public funds. **Vijay** emphasized that he would not tolerate any wrongdoing within his administration and vowed to prioritize the welfare of all citizens, including women, youth, farmers, and minorities.

recent_articles.title: Stalin reacts to Tamil Nadu CM Vijay speech: ‘Money is there; what is required is efficient administration’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **M.K. Stalin**, former Tamil Nadu Chief Minister and DMK president, criticized **C. Joseph Vijay's** statement that the previous government left the state treasury empty with a debt burden of ₹10 lakh crore.  Stalin asserted that the government should not claim there was "no money" at the beginning of its tenure, suggesting instead that an efficient administration is needed to distribute existing resources.

recent_articles.title: Tamil Nadu swearing-in ceremony LIVE: TVK president C. Joseph Vijay arrives at venue - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **C. Joseph Vijay**, president of the **Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)**, will be sworn in as the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu on Sunday, May 10, 2026.  He secured the support of 120 MLAs-elect after a nail-biting political uncertainty that ended with the **VCK** and the **IUML** extending their support to the TVK coalition government. The swearing-in ceremony will take place at Nehru Stadium in Chennai at 10 a.m.
